topics.theatre: Theatre closure and performance during the Interregnum

levelNote: Conceptual questions on the Commonwealth, Protectorate, major writers, literary works, political context and theatre suppression.

questions.question: Which sequence is chronologically correct?
options: Theatre order, execution of Charles I, Protectorate, Restoration
Execution of Charles I, Restoration, theatre order, Protectorate
Restoration, Protectorate, theatre order, execution of Charles I
Protectorate, theatre order, Restoration, execution of Charles I
questions.explanation: The dates are 1642, 1649, 1653 and 1660 respectively.

questions.question: The Rump Parliament's declaration of the Commonwealth in May 1649 followed which event?
questions.explanation: The execution had occurred in January 1649.

questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes the Commonwealth from the Protectorate?
options: The Commonwealth began in 1660; the Protectorate began in 1642
The Commonwealth restored Charles II; the Protectorate elected James II
The Commonwealth began as a republic; the Protectorate placed a Lord Protector at its head
questions.explanation: The Protectorate began in 1653 under Cromwell.

questions.question: Which document offered a written constitutional framework for Cromwell's rule?
questions.explanation: The Instrument of Government was adopted in 1653.

questions.question: Who ruled briefly after Oliver Cromwell before the Stuart Restoration?
questions.explanation: Richard Cromwell inherited the office of Lord Protector.

questions.question: The word Interregnum in this context refers to which situation?
options: A union of Scotland and France
A period of two simultaneous kings
An interval without a reigning monarch
questions.explanation: England lacked a king from 1649 until 1660.

questions.question: Which body directly preceded Cromwell's dissolution of Parliament in April 1653?
questions.explanation: Cromwell forcibly dissolved the Rump in April 1653.

questions.question: The Restoration of 1660 brought which dynasty back to the throne?
questions.explanation: Charles II belonged to the Stuart dynasty.

questions.question: Which pairing is historically accurate?
questions.explanation: The Commonwealth was proclaimed in 1649.

questions.question: Which is the most accurate description of Parliament's 1642 order on stage plays?
options: It suspended public plays during the Civil War before the Commonwealth existed
It first applied only after Cromwell's death
It permanently banned all writing for the stage
questions.explanation: The 1642 ordinance preceded the republic by seven years.

questions.question: What makes Milton's Areopagitica especially significant?
options: It argues against prior licensing of printed works
It is an allegorical masque about chastity
questions.explanation: Milton's prose tract opposes pre-publication censorship.

questions.question: Which pairing correctly identifies Milton's work and genre?
questions.explanation: Samson Agonistes is a tragedy intended primarily for reading.

questions.question: What central theological event structures Paradise Lost?
questions.explanation: The epic narrates temptation and the Fall.

questions.question: What is a principal purpose Milton announces for Paradise Lost?
options: To justify the ways of God to humanity
questions.explanation: Milton frames the epic as an exploration of divine justice.

questions.question: Which pair of Milton's works appeared together in 1671?
options: Eikonoklastes and The Tenure of Kings and Magistrates
questions.explanation: The two were issued together in 1671.

questions.question: Which work did Milton write in response to royalist Eikon Basilike?
questions.explanation: Eikonoklastes attacked the image of Charles I presented by Eikon Basilike.

questions.question: Which public role did Milton hold under the Commonwealth?
questions.explanation: He served the Council of State from 1649.

questions.question: Why is the verse of Paradise Lost called blank verse?
options: It is written as prose paragraphs
Every line ends in a rhyming couplet
questions.explanation: Blank verse has metre without end rhyme.

questions.question: Which description best fits Lycidas?
options: A pastoral elegy for Edward King
questions.explanation: It uses pastoral convention to lament a death.

questions.question: Which pair represents Milton's contrasting early companion poems?
questions.explanation: The pair contrast mirth and contemplative melancholy.

questions.question: Which literary device chiefly structures the argument in To His Coy Mistress?
options: A pastoral lament for a dead poet
A formal debate over divine right
A carpe diem appeal based on the brevity of life
questions.explanation: The speaker uses limited time to urge immediate love.

questions.question: Which poem weighs Cromwell's political rise against the fall of Charles I?
options: An Horatian Ode upon Cromwell's Return from Ireland
questions.explanation: The Horatian ode responds to revolutionary politics with complex judgement.

questions.question: Which Marvell poem is associated with the Fairfax family and Nun Appleton?
options: The Nymph Complaining for the Death of Her Fawn
questions.explanation: Upon Appleton House explores the Fairfax estate and its meanings.

questions.question: What does Marvell's The Garden notably explore?
options: The appeal of solitude and contemplative retreat
questions.explanation: The Garden meditates on solitude, nature and the mind.

questions.question: Which contrast is especially important in To His Coy Mistress?
options: Boundless imagined courtship versus the pressure of mortal time
questions.explanation: The poem contrasts a hypothetical eternity with imminent death.

questions.question: The tone of An Horatian Ode is best described as what?
questions.explanation: The poem registers both Cromwell's energy and the king's dignity.

questions.question: Which problem does Hobbes's social contract address in Leviathan?
options: How people escape insecurity without a common power
How a fisherman should select bait
questions.explanation: The covenant gives authority to a sovereign for peace.

questions.question: What is the key political function of the sovereign in Hobbes's theory?
questions.explanation: The sovereign's authority restrains violent conflict.

questions.question: Which statement most closely reflects Hobbes's view of the state of nature?
options: It is identical to the Restoration court
It is a system governed by elected judges
It is a guaranteed era of stable peace
Without common authority, conflict and insecurity threaten human life
questions.explanation: The state of nature lacks a common power to keep people in awe.

questions.question: Why is Leviathan a fitting title for Hobbes's political treatise?
options: It refers to Milton's central angel
It presents a powerful commonwealth as an artificial political body
It names a Stuart court theatre
It describes a pastoral poem about a fish
questions.explanation: Hobbes uses the figure of Leviathan for sovereign common power.

questions.question: Which Browne work investigates common errors and accepted false beliefs?
questions.explanation: Pseudodoxia Epidemica examines vulgar errors.

questions.question: Hydriotaphia most directly meditates on which theme?
questions.explanation: Urn-Burial considers death and posterity.

questions.question: Which pair of Browne's works was published together in 1658?
options: Hydriotaphia and The Garden of Cyrus
The Compleat Angler and The Mistress
questions.explanation: The two treatises were published in 1658.

questions.question: What distinctive combination characterises Religio Medici?
options: A dialogue about fishing and nature
Personal faith and reflective enquiry from a physician's perspective
Epic blank verse and a biblical Fall
questions.explanation: The work mingles religious self-examination and learned reflection.

questions.question: Which of these correctly pairs author and work?
options: Sir Thomas Browne: The Garden of Cyrus
questions.explanation: The Garden of Cyrus belongs to Browne.

questions.question: How is The Compleat Angler best described?
options: A biblical epic in blank verse
A dialogue blending fishing instruction with reflection on rural life
questions.explanation: The book combines practical angling with a contemplative outlook.

questions.question: Which writer's Life was written by Izaak Walton?
questions.explanation: Walton's biographical Lives include Donne.

questions.question: Which contrast best distinguishes Walton's prose from Hobbes's Leviathan?
options: Walton explores contemplative recreation; Hobbes analyses political sovereignty
Walton writes a constitutional theory; Hobbes composes devotional lyrics
questions.explanation: The works have very different prose purposes.

questions.question: Which of these authors is associated with biographies of Richard Hooker and George Herbert?
questions.explanation: Walton included Hooker and Herbert among his Lives.

questions.question: Which collection best represents Henry Vaughan's religious metaphysical verse?
questions.explanation: Silex Scintillans is Vaughan's chief devotional collection.

questions.question: Which earlier poet's The Temple was a major model for Vaughan's Silex Scintillans?
questions.explanation: Vaughan drew extensively on Herbert's religious verse.

questions.question: In Vaughan's The Retreat, childhood chiefly suggests what?
options: A state of spiritual nearness or innocence
questions.explanation: The poem idealizes a childhood closer to the divine.

questions.question: Which pair gives the publication dates of the two editions of Silex Scintillans?
questions.explanation: Vaughan expanded the collection in 1655.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects Vaughan's religious poetry during the Interregnum?
options: It sustains Anglican devotion amid political and ecclesiastical change
It chiefly dramatizes comedies for public theatres
It praises theatrical licensing as its main theme
questions.explanation: His writing preserves Anglican faith through devotional verse.

questions.question: What was Cowley's Davideis intended to recount?
questions.explanation: Davideis is an unfinished epic on David.

questions.question: What distinguishes Cowley's Pindaric odes in English practice?
options: Exclusive use of Old English alliteration
Irregular stanzaic patterns inspired by Pindar
questions.explanation: Cowley popularised free or irregular Pindaric structures.

questions.question: Which Cowley collection is chiefly linked with love poetry?
questions.explanation: The Mistress contains Cowley's love poems.

questions.question: Which work appeared in Cowley's Poems of 1656 and helped popularize the Pindaric mode?
questions.explanation: Cowley's 1656 volume included Pindarique Odes.

questions.question: Why is it misleading to say that Cromwell first closed English theatres in 1649?
options: Theatres were never regulated in the seventeenth century
The first theatre order came after the Restoration
The initial theatre closure was ordered by Charles II
Parliament had ordered public plays to cease in 1642, before Cromwell's Protectorate
questions.explanation: The 1642 ordinance predates Cromwell's 1653 Protectorate.

questions.question: Which statement about performance during the Interregnum is most accurate?
options: No theatrical writing or performance survived
Official restrictions existed, but performances did not disappear completely
Every London theatre operated legally without interruption
questions.explanation: Scholars document illicit performances and alternative entertainment forms.
